 Dylan Harper (groin) exited Tuesday’s loss to the Spurs with 53.6 seconds left in the fourth quarter.
 Harper slipped and did a split while running down the court late in the fourth quarter, forcing a premature end to his night. Although he got back to his feet, the Spurs guard needed help walking to the locker room. Harper finished with 20 points (8-of-14 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), four rebounds and two assists. The Spurs host the Clippers on Thursday, and a spot start could be in the cards for Julian Champagnie (14 points, six rebounds, one block and four three-pointers).
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 De’Aaron Fox (hip) is not on the injury report for Tuesday’s game against the Pistons. 
 After playing 17 minutes in Friday’s blowout win over the Warriors, Fox did not play in Sunday’s win over the Jazz. He was replaced in the starting lineup by Julian Champagnie, who will return to the bench on Tuesday. Fox’s return also means slightly lower usage rates for Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper finished Sunday’s win over the Jazz with 31 points (12-of-23 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers. 
 After scoring 19 points or fewer in five straight and six of San Antonio’s first seven games of November, Harper had one of the best games of his young NBA career on Sunday. The second-year guard recorded his first 30-point game as a pro while finishing one rebound shy of a double-double. Harper has been a reliable fantasy option this season, and De’Aaron Fox (hip) not playing on Sunday raised his ceiling.

 De’Aaron Fox (hip) is questionable to play against the Warriors on Friday. 
 Fox could end up missing a game for the first time this season. If that happens, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle would likely see a bump in usage. Devin Vassell has been sidelined but is questionable as well. If he returns and Fox is out, Julian Champagnie will continue to start. If both are out, Keldon Johnson or Carter Bryant could enter the starting lineup. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper finished Wednesday’s win over the Bulls with 18 points (7-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, 10 assists, four steals, one block and two three-pointers. 
 With his father Ron, who won three NBA titles with the Bulls in the mid-90s, in attendance, Harper had another solid showing on Wednesday. The second-year guard recorded his first career double-double, dishing out 10 assists and scoring 18 points. While Harper’s field-goal percentage left a bit to be desired, he didn’t commit a turnover in his 36 minutes. Closing in on top-50 value in nine-cat formats, Harper is currently outperforming his ADP (80).
